# Branch activation and first rider setup

Draft branch details now offer Review activation. The sheet reads the existing onboarding activation-readiness endpoint, displays actual blockers, and enables Request activation only when ready. Blocked users can open business setup and return to the branch. The request uses the existing request-activation endpoint, then rereads the branch before displaying success. Activation applies business-wide to eligible draft branches/capabilities; the sheet explains that scope. It preserves the backend onboarding-read/manage permissions, compliance/verification evaluation, idempotency and prohibition on activating a draft through Resume. No direct branch activation backend or new approval policy has been added.

GET /api/v1/vendor/delivery/rider/branches supplies paginated minimal branch IDs/display names. It requires execute-assigned delivery permission, its branch scope, active current staff, a live Vendor Rider role assignment covering the branch, and an active branch belonging to the same vendor. It does not grant general branch-list or settings access. Rider availability setup now uses this endpoint instead of the business settings list. Empty/denied branches block new setup with guidance; pending command recovery retains the original frozen request.

Existing availability GET can return FULFILMENT_NOT_FOUND for a first-time rider. The controller then sends the first PUT with If-Match 0, followed by the persisted positive version on later changes. Existing eligibility, busy-mission protection and version checks remain server-owned. The new route needs deployment with the frontend; an older backend will not provide its branch picker.

Mock adds First rider setup in the existing scenario selector. It starts with no current-user mission or availability record and uses the same first-write version semantics. Saved branch activation checks each branch's Location projection and updates eligible draft records through the existing activation request. New unverified branches remain Draft. Preapproved fixture branches can activate; Mock does not invent an approval action.

Focused validation covers first-write/update versions, invalid branch refusal, unverified draft refusal, approved draft activation and the existing assigned-rider sequence. Backend rider package checks, analyzer and generated contract verification are focused checks, not deployment/database/device certification. Live verification remains item 5.
